title: Candy
statement: Children stand in a line with ratings. Each gets at least one candy, and a child with a higher rating than an immediate neighbour gets more candies than that neighbour. Return the minimum total.
hints: Each child has two constraints: from the left neighbour and from the right.
Satisfy left constraints in a left-to-right pass, right constraints in a right-to-left pass, keeping the max.

solution.explanation: Split the constraints. A left-to-right pass gives the minimum satisfying every "higher than my left neighbour" rule; a right-to-left pass does the same for right neighbours; taking the max satisfies both, and each value is forced (it's the length of the increasing run ending there from each side), so it's minimal. "Two passes, one direction each" also solves trapping rain water and product of array except self.
